OD-B01-S01.text: The gods take their places in a widening ring.
How mortals love to blame the gods for their sorrows.
Think of Aegisthus, who took Agamemnon's wife and cut the king down at his homecoming,
though we sent Hermes himself to warn him.
His own recklessness doubled the fate he was owed.
Father Zeus, let Aegisthus lie in the ruin he earned.
It is Odysseus my heart breaks for, wise, unlucky Odysseus, held against his will on Calypso's island,
longing only for the sight of smoke rising from his own hearth.
Has he not paid you sacrifice enough on the plain of Troy, Olympian?
My child, how could I forget godlike Odysseus?
It is Poseidon the earth-shaker who rages without rest for the blinding of his Cyclops son,
and drives that man from his homecoming.
But come, let us here shape his return;
one god cannot hold out against us all.

OD-B01-S02.text: Then send Hermes, the guide, the slayer of Argus, across the water to Ogygia at once.
Let him stand before the nymph Calypso with our fixed decree:
And I go to Ithaca myself, to breathe strength into his son.
I will set Telemachus on his feet, send him to call the Achaeans to assembly,
and then across the sea to Pylos and Sparta for news of his father, so the boy may win a name among men.
So the gods divided the labor:
release the father, waken the son.
Two roads laid down at once, bending toward a single homecoming.
Athena fastens the gold sandals, closes her hand around the spear, and drops from Olympus.

OD-B01-S03.text: Wearing the shape of Mentes, Athena waits at the palace threshold with her spear upright.
the suitors never look toward the gate.
Telemachus sees the unattended stranger and crosses the hall, ashamed of his own house.
You are kindly come to our house;
Eat first, and afterward tell me what you need, but come, away from this noise.

OD-B01-S04.text: Telemachus gives the stranger the chair of honor and sits close enough to keep the conversation private.
They devour another man's substance without payment, a man whose white bones lie rotting in the rain somewhere,
or rolling in the salt surf.
If he had fallen at Troy I could bear it;
instead these men eat my house to nothing, and soon enough they will tear me apart as well.
I am Mentes, son of wise Anchialus, lord of the oar-loving Taphians, and your father's guest-friend of old;
ask grizzled Laertes if you doubt it.
He is held on a sea-girt island by rough men, and he will contrive his way home,
for no man alive is richer in devices.
But tell me truly, are you Odysseus's own son?
Your head, your fine eyes, you are marvelously like him as I knew him.
And what is this feast, this mob filling the house?
For no man of sense could stomach such insolence under his own roof.

OD-B01-S05.text: My mother neither refuses a marriage she hates nor makes an end of the matter.
So from Dulichium and Same and wooded Zacynthus, and from rocky Ithaca itself, they come courting her,
and day by day they grind my house to nothing.
Oh, for Odysseus at that doorway now, helmet and shield and his two spears,
the man I first knew in our house drinking and glad.
A bitter, brief wooing they would find;
their deaths would come down on every one of them like night.
Now hear me, and do it.
Tomorrow call the Achaean lords to assembly and bid the suitors scatter, each man to his own home.
Then fit out a ship of twenty oars and go for news of your long-gone father, to Nestor at Pylos first,
then to sandy Sparta and red-haired Menelaus, the last of the bronze-clad Achaeans home.
Have you not heard what fame Orestes won among men, striking down the schemer who murdered his famous father?
You are tall and well-made, my friend;
be brave, so that men born after you will speak your name.

OD-B01-S06.text: Do not hold me longer, my road calls.
Whatever gift your heart bids you give, keep it for my homeward passing, and it will be repaid with its equal.
The goddess rises like a bird;
Telemachus returns to the hall with his posture changed.
Phemius, break off this bitter song, it wastes my heart in my breast.
sing the deeds of men and gods, but not the Achaeans' coming home.
Mother, let the singer sing as his mind moves him;
Odysseus is not the only man who never came home from Troy.
Go up to your rooms and tend your own work, the loom and the distaff;
speech will be the concern of men, and mine above all, for the authority in this house is mine.
And at dawn I call the assembly.
Night sealed the household, but Telemachus lay awake inside the course Athena had set.

OD-B02-S01.text: Summon the long-haired Achaeans to assembly at first light, every man of them.
He enters with two hounds and takes the seat that belonged to his father.
Not once since great Odysseus sailed in the hollow ships have we met in council.
What man had such need, young or old?
Has he word of the army coming home?
Whoever he is, blessings on him for it.
Old sir, that man is not far to seek:
I called you, and the trouble is mine.
I have lost my noble father, who was king among you here and gentle as a father;
and now a greater ruin besides, suitors who beset my mother against her will and devour my house day after day.
By Olympian Zeus and by Themis who seats the councils of men, I call it wrong, and I cannot fight it alone.

OD-B02-S02.text: Bold-tongued Telemachus, do not lay your blame at our door.
It is not the suitors who are at fault but your own mother, that queen of cunning;
three years now, and nearly four, she has cheated the hearts of the Achaeans.
She set up her great loom in the hall, a shroud, she told us, for the lord Laertes,
so no woman of the land could reproach her if he lay in death without a winding-sheet.
All day she wove at that web, and every night, with torches set beside her, she unraveled it thread by thread.
We caught her at the loom and forced the web to its end.
Send her back to her father Icarius, and let her marry the man he names, and the man she chooses.

OD-B02-S03.text: Antinous, I will never drive from this house the mother who bore me and raised me,
not while my father lives or lies dead far away.
feast somewhere else, eat your own stores house to house.
Or stay and devour on, and I will cry to the gods who live forever that a day of reckoning come,
and you die in this house unavenged.
Two eagles descend, wheel over the assembly, and tear at one another before vanishing inland.
Odysseus is not long from his people now;
he is near, already sowing death and doom for these men.
I read the birds for him the day he sailed, twenty years from home, all his companions lost,
himself unknown at his return, and it is coming to pass.
Let us stop the suitors now, before the ruin falls on more than them.
Old man, go home and prophesy to your children.
Birds are forever crossing the sunlight, and not all of them mean anything.
Odysseus is dead far away, and a pity you did not die with him.
Keep pouring out omens and goading this angry boy, and your prophecy will cost you a fine you will weep to pay.

OD-B02-S04.text: Give me a swift ship and twenty companions,
for I go to Pylos and to Sparta seeking news of my father so long away.
If I hear he lives and is coming home, I can hold out one year more;
if I hear he is dead, I will raise his mound, pay him all the honors owed, and give my mother to a husband.
Hear me now, men of Ithaca.
Let no sceptered king ever again be kind and gentle, since none of you remembers godlike Odysseus,
who ruled you mild as a father.
I do not begrudge the proud suitors their violence, they wager their own heads on it.
It is you I blame, the many, who sit here dumb and never say one word to shame a few.
Mentor, you crazed old rabble-baiter, would you rouse the town against us?
Fighting men over a dinner is grim work.
if Ithacan Odysseus himself came home and found us feasting in his hall and set his heart on driving us out,
his wife would have small joy of the husband she longs for;
he would meet an ugly death then and there, one man against so many.
Go back to your fields, all of you.
Citizens disperse and the suitors return to the palace.

OD-B02-S05.text: Hear me, god who came yesterday to our house and bade me sail the misty sea for news of my father's return.
All of it the Achaeans thwart, and the suitors first, in their evil insolence.
Telemachus, you will prove no coward and no fool hereafter,
if one drop of your father's fine spirit is truly in you.
That man made word and deed agree, and so will you;
I sailed with your father of old, and I will sail with you, and find you a swift ship besides.
Go home now, and move among the suitors as if nothing has changed.
Make ready the stores, wine in two-handled jars and barley meal in tight skins, the marrow of men.
I will gather a willing crew through the town and choose the best ship in sea-girt Ithaca,
and we launch her on the dark water tonight.
The voyage becomes a hidden operation running beneath the suitors' gaze.

OD-B02-S06.text: Antinous, take your hand from mine.
Am I to feast in quiet among you who strip my house bare?
I will make my voyage to Pylos, as a passenger on another man's deck if I must,
and I will bring ruin home to you if the gods grant it.
Telemachus enters the locked storeroom filled with metal, cloth, oil, wine, and meal.
Nurse, draw me twelve jars of wine, the finest after what you keep for that unlucky man,
And pour twenty measures of milled barley into stitched skins.
Have it gathered by nightfall, and no one is to know, least of all my mother until I am gone.
Ah, child, why has this thought come into your heart?
You are an only son, beloved, and the sea will eat you as it ate him;
stay and keep what is yours.
But since you will go, I swear it by the gods:
your mother hears nothing from me till the twelfth day, unless she misses you and asks herself.

OD-B02-S07.text: Athena, disguised as Telemachus, recruits crewmen and borrows Noemon's ship.
Your companions sit at the oars already, waiting on your word;
let us not delay the voyage.
The crew carries provisions from the palace and stows them below deck.
Athena takes the pilot's seat and sends a strong west wind.
The sail fills, libations are poured, and the ship travels through the night.

OD-B03-S01.text: At sunrise the ship reaches Pylos, where nine great divisions sacrifice black bulls to Poseidon.
How do I even greet such a man?
I have no practice in careful speech.
Telemachus, no more shyness, not now;
you crossed the sea for your father's sake.
Go straight up to Nestor, breaker of horses, and ask him what counsel he keeps in his breast.
Some words you will find in yourself, and a god will set the rest on your tongue,
for the gods have not left you unattended from your birth.
Come inside, take food, and speak when you are ready.
Hear me, Poseidon, girdler of the earth.
Grant fame to Nestor and his sons, grace to all Pylos in return for this rich hecatomb,
and grant that Telemachus and I accomplish the errand we sailed here to do.

OD-B03-S02.text: Strangers, now that you have had your pleasure of the feast, it is fair to ask:
From where do you sail the watery ways?
Is it on business, or do you rove at hazard like raiders,
who risk their own lives to bring evil upon other men?
Nestor, son of Neleus, great glory of the Achaeans, we come from Ithaca below Neion, and the errand is my own:
my father, hard-enduring Odysseus, who fought at your side and sacked the city of Troy.
I beg you, do not soften anything out of pity for me;
tell me exactly what your own eyes saw or what word has reached you.
Friend, you bring it all back, what we suffered on that plain, and the best of us fallen:
Ajax lies there, and Achilles, and Patroclus wise as the gods, and my own strong Antilochus.
And in every craft of war your father had no rival;
no man alive could match Odysseus for cunning.
Truly you are his son, your very speech is his.
Nestor begins the account of the quarrel that split the returning Greek fleet.

OD-B03-S03.text: The two sons of Atreus called the army to assembly at sunset, a reckless hour,
and stood and quarreled before us all.
Menelaus said sail, sail now over the sea's broad back;
Agamemnon would hold the host and slaughter hecatombs to appease Athena's wrath.
Fool, for she was not to be turned so, and we split in two, and the night was ugly with shouting.
Odysseus turned back to support Agamemnon.
Nestor, Diomedes, and Menelaus escaped by a difficult route and reached home.
But of Odysseus I can tell you only what has drifted to my hearth, for I came home with no news of my own.
They say the Myrmidons came safe, and Philoctetes, and Idomeneus lost not a man the war had spared;
but of your father, living or dead, no traveler has brought me one certain word.

OD-B03-S04.text: You know how Aegisthus, while we bled at Troy, sat safe in horse-pasturing Argos and charmed Agamemnon's wife,
and how he cut the king down at his own hearth on the day of his homecoming.
in the eighth year Orestes returned from Athens and killed his father's murderer,
and all the Argives honored him for the deed.
And you, my friend, tall and fine as I see you are, be brave, so that men not yet born will speak well of you.
Do not wander long away from home while those proud men sit in your halls and eat everything you have.
If only the gods would give me strength like that.
But they will not, not for me, not for my father.
Telemachus, what word has escaped the barrier of your teeth?
Easily, when he wills it, a god brings a man safe home from the ends of the earth.
Better long roads and hard travel and a late return than to come home swiftly and die at your own hearth,

OD-B03-S05.text: Night approaches and Nestor invites the guests to his palace.
Go with him, Telemachus, and sleep at the king's house.
But I will back to the ship, to hearten the crew, for I am the one old man among them;
and at dawn I go on to the Cauconians, where a debt is owed me, no new thing and no small one.
Dear boy, no fear that you prove base or weak, when gods walk beside you so young,
and that was no other of the Olympians but the daughter of Zeus himself,
the glorious grey-eyed one who honored your father among the Argives.
grant fair fame to me, to my children, to my honored wife, and I will sacrifice to you a yearling heifer,
broad-browed, unbroken, her horns wrapped in gold.
At dawn a heifer is sacrificed.
Telemachus is bathed and dressed for departure.

OD-B03-S06.text: Quickly now, my sons, harness the flowing-maned horses to the car for Telemachus,
and let the housekeeper load bread and wine and such meats as kings' sons feed on.
He has far to drive before nightfall.
Pisistratus takes the reins beside him and drives out of Pylos.
Pisistratus spend the night at Phera under Diocles's hospitality.
At first light they yoked the horses again and drove out through gate and ringing portico,
all day through the wheatlands, until the sun sank and every road grew dark toward Lacedaemon.

OD-B04-S01.text: Telemachus and Pisistratus reach Menelaus's palace during a double wedding feast.
Attendants unharness the horses, bathe the guests, and seat them at the feast.
bronze flashing through the echoing halls, gold and amber, silver and ivory.
Surely the court of Zeus on Olympus is like this;
wonder takes me just to look.

OD-B04-S02.text: Yet for no man of them all do I grieve as for Odysseus, who labored at Troy beyond us all.
His absence is sorrow to old Laertes, to steady Penelope, and to Telemachus,
the child he left new-born in his hall.
Menelaus, shall I speak what my eyes tell me?
Never have I seen such likeness in man or woman —
the son Odysseus left a baby at home when for my shameless sake the Achaeans sailed to Troy.
Pisistratus confirms the identity and recalls his own dead brother Antilochus.
we shame the feast with weeping.
with dawn there will be time for all our tales, and tears enough to go with them.

OD-B04-S03.text: Helen mixes a drug into the wine that quiets grief and anger.
Hear one deed of that man of endurance.
He scarred his own flesh with blows, threw a beggar's rags across his back,
and walked through the gates of Troy —
into the city of his enemies, looking like a slave.
Helen alone recognized and bathed him.
Only when I had sworn a great oath not to name him did he open to me the whole design of the Achaeans.
Odysseus killed Trojans and returned to the ships with intelligence.

OD-B04-S04.text: Hear the horse's tale from within:
I crouched in that timber belly with the best of the Argives, and Odysseus held command of us all,
when you came circling in the dark.
Helen circled the horse and imitated the voices of the warriors' wives.
Odysseus restrained them and silenced Anticlus.
Telemachus hears proof of his father's endurance and command under pressure.

OD-B04-S05.text: Son of Atreus, royal Menelaus, I came for this alone:
tell me plainly of my father Odysseus.
Did you hear that he lives, or must I mourn him?
Do not soften it out of pity —
tell me what your own eyes have met.
The gods held me windbound off Egypt, on the isle of Pharos, till hunger gnawed my crews —
until Eidothea, daughter of the sea's old man,
pitied me and taught me how to seize her father Proteus and wring the truth from him.
Menelaus and three men hid beneath sealskins and grappled the Old Man of the Sea.
Which of the gods taught you this trap, son of Atreus?
What do you want of me?
One more I saw, shedding great tears on an island:
Odysseus, held in the halls of the nymph Calypso,
with no ship and no companions to carry him over the sea's broad back.

OD-B04-S06.text: Stay with me a month, Telemachus, and I will send you off with horses and a shining chariot —
or does your heart already pull you home?
No horses, then, for rocky Ithaca —
a mixing bowl of wrought silver, its lip finished in gold, the work of Hephaestus himself.
And this gift from me, dear child —
a robe my own hands wove.
Let it lie in your mother's keeping until your wedding day, and let your bride wear the memory of Helen.
As the chariot rolls from the gate an eagle sweeps by on the right, a white goose in its talons —
and Helen cries out the sign:
so shall Odysseus, long away, swoop home upon the feasters in his hall and take his payment.

OD-B04-S07.text: When Telemachus will return your ship?
The suitors discover that the voyage truly occurred without their knowledge.
Antinous selects a crew and sails to the strait between Ithaca and Same to ambush the prince.
Queen, forgive the word I carry:

some god lulled the waves to sleep —
and ahead lay the island of the Sirens.
Ears to me, each man in turn —
this wax stays till we are long past that shore.
They bound him hand and foot, upright in the mast-step,
and beat the sea white beneath their oars past the flowering shore.
Odysseus struggles and signals to be released.
But Perimedes and Eurylochus rose and lashed him tighter still,
and the crew rowed until the song sank beneath the sound of the sea.

OD-B12-S04.text: The crew hears Charybdis roar and sees spray rising from the whirlpool.
we have been in worse and lived, and this too we shall remember.
Helmsman, hold her off that smoke and hug the cliff —
keep to the rock, or you kill us all.
Odysseus arms himself despite Circe's warning and searches the rock face.
Scylla's six heads strike, lifting six screaming men from the ship.
The survivors pass beyond both monsters while watching their companions die above them.

OD-B12-S05.text: The exhausted crew sees the cattle and sheep of Helios on Thrinacia.
Tiresias and Circe both warned me alike:
our worst harm waits on that island.
Call me merciless if you will, Eurylochus —
The men swear to touch no livestock and land for one night.
A month of storm winds traps them while stores diminish.
Odysseus repeatedly reminds them of the oath.

OD-B12-S06.text: When the last of Circe's stores was gone, Odysseus went up-island to pray the gods for a road home —
and they poured sweet sleep over his eyelids.
Eurylochus persuades the crew to sacrifice the best cattle rather than starve.
Eurylochus substitute oak leaves for barley and water for wine, kill the animals, and roast the meat.
The hides crawl and the meat bellows on the spits.
Lampetie tells Helios, who demands punishment from Zeus.

OD-B12-S07.text: you have slaughtered the Sun's own herds while I slept!
O father Zeus, you lulled me to my ruin.
This is doom, and no offering on earth will unmake it.
Six days they feasted on the finest of the cattle;
on the seventh the storm-wind fell, and they stepped the mast and stood out to open sea.
Zeus gathers a black cloud and strikes the mast with lightning.
The ship shatters and every crewman drowns.
Odysseus lashes keel and mast together.
Driven back to Charybdis, he hangs from the fig tree until the timbers reemerge, then drifts alone to Calypso.

OD-B13-S01.text: My story is told, and the telling has emptied me.
Bring out one more chest, and let every lord of Phaeacia add a tripod and a cauldron to it.
Then set the feast, for our guest sails at sundown and he must leave us glad.
At sunset Odysseus boards the convoy ship and lies on a prepared bed in the stern.
Swifter than a wheeling hawk the ship ran on,
and the man who had suffered twenty years of salt and war slept past all sorrow.
Before the dawn-star rose, her keel touched Ithaca.
The crew carries the sleeping man and his treasure onto the shore.

OD-B13-S02.text: The ship is gone, and even the land has hidden its face from me.
Tripods, cauldrons, the woven robes, the gold.
All of it here, nothing taken.
Then why does this shore know nothing of me, unless those sailors dumped me on some foreign coast?
Wretched again, and among strangers again.
O Zeus, where do I carry all this wealth, and where do I carry myself?
Stranger, why do you wander this coast with treasure at your feet and fear in your eyes?

OD-B13-S03.text: The shepherd tells Odysseus you is in Ithaca and the hero suppresses your joy.
He invents a Cretan identity and a story of killing a king's son and fleeing by Phoenician ship.
Cunning, insatiable trickster, even in your own land you will not lay your lies aside!
I am Athena, daughter of Zeus, and we two are alike, crooked-minded both,
you the best of mortals at scheming and I of gods.
Hard goddess, where were you all the salt years since Troy burned?
You stood at my shoulder then, and after, I never once saw you on my deck while I suffered.
Now you come smiling and tell me this is Ithaca, so swear it is not one more mockery.
So that is the shape of it.
Poseidon's wrath made open rescue too costly, and you wore silence the way I wear rags.
You hid me even from my own eyes to keep me breathing.

OD-B13-S04.text: Your bronze and gold will keep better here than on any beach.
No thief alive will shift that stone.
Now sit with me under the olive, and let us plot.
Athena count the suitors and devise a concealment strategy.
Go first to your swineherd Eumaeus, keeper of your pigs and lover of your house,
and stay by his fire and question everything.
I go to Sparta, to fetch your son home.

OD-B13-S05.text: Athena touches Odysseus with her wand and shrivels his skin, hair, and limbs.
Dimmed eyes, wracked limbs, rags fit for burning on an old man's back.
No one who ever loved you will look at you twice.
Take this staff and this patched beggar's sack, for this is who you are now.
The transformed king is instructed to test servants without being recognized.
Walk on, old beggar, and keep to the high path.

OD-B14-S01.text: Smoke, and the smell of pigs.
Someone keeps this hill better than the palace keeps itself.
Out of the yard four dogs came at him like wolves, and the man dropped his staff and sat down in the dirt,
old soldier's craft, letting their fury break over a harmless thing.
Old man, another moment and you'd have been torn, and the shame of it mine forever.
Sit, grandfather, here, my own seat by the fire.
Two young pigs I'll dress for us;
eat first, and tell your griefs after.

OD-B14-S02.text: Forgive the poor meat, old man;
young pork is all the suitors leave us.
The fattened boars go down the mountain to men who eat a lost king's herds and fear no god watching.
My master, and I will say his name, Odysseus, was kind to me past any telling, and the sea has him now,
Every drifter who wants supper sings me a tale that he lives.
Then hear an oath, not a song.
By Zeus of guests, by this table and this fire:
Odysseus comes home before this year is out.
When he stands in his own hall, give me a cloak and tunic then, and not one hour before.
Keep your oath, friend, for I'll pay no cloak on it, and Odysseus will not come.
Drink your wine and speak of other things;
my heart aches enough whenever his name is said.

OD-B14-S03.text: But you now, who are you, and from where among men?
What ship brought you, and what grief?
For no man walks to Ithaca.
Crete, then Troy, then Egypt in chains, go on, leave nothing out.
And this Thesprotian king, say again what he swore to you about Odysseus and the treasure coming home.
true harbors, true wars, true hunger, and a false name at the keel.
The lie is a net, cast gently, to sound the depth of the swineherd's heart.
Poor man, your wanderings wring my heart, and every word of hardship I believe.
But the word about Odysseus, no.
Why do you good men think a lie will comfort me?

OD-B14-S04.text: Night turns cold and wet as Eumaeus's herdsmen return.
Hear a boast from an old soldier, since wine loosens me.
One freezing ambush-night at Troy I lay without a cloak,
and Odysseus spun a trick on the spot that got one onto my shoulders.
Ah, to be that young man tonight, someone in this hut might do the same.
Well hinted, old man, and no fault in the hint.
Here, my spare cloak, sleep warm.
Eumaeus sleeps near the pigs himself, guarding the herd through the storm.

OD-B15-S01.text: It is wrong to wander while your house is eaten hollow.
before your mother's own kin bend her to marry Eurymachus and your inheritance walks out the door with her.
the boldest of the suitors lie in ambush in the strait between Ithaca and rocky Same,
hungry for your blood before you ever reach home.
Keep clear of that channel, sail wide, and sail by night.
When you touch Ithaca, send ship and crew round to the town without you.
Go first, on foot, to the swineherd Eumaeus, who keeps faith with your house;
sleep there, and send him to tell your mother you are safely home.
Telemachus wakes Pisistratus and prepares to depart at dawn.

OD-B15-S02.text: Menelaus, dear to Zeus, your gifts honor me and I take them gladly.
But do not hold me for more feasting;
my heart is already on Ithaca, and I fear what rots there while I linger.
Take this robe, child, woven by my own hands, for the bride you will one day wed;
let your mother keep it till then.
And read that eagle with the white goose in its claws as I do:
so Odysseus, home from long wandering, will stoop upon the suitors, or he is home already, seeding their ruin.
So the whips came down and the horses flew, through Phera as the sun set, and on to sandy Pylos with the dawn.
Son of Nestor, will you do me one kindness more, and drive me past your father's gates,
Old Nestor's welcome is warm, but it does not let go, and I cannot lose a night to it.

OD-B15-S03.text: Aboard, men, rig the mast and run out the oars.
We sail for home now, not at dawn.
Friend, by your sacrifice and by the god you pour to, tell me truly who you are, and then hear me.
I have killed a kinsman in Argos, and his brothers hunt my life across the islands.
Take me aboard, for I am a suppliant and a seer, and I have nowhere on this earth to stand.
I will not push away a man who asks.
you'll share what we have, and in Ithaca you will be made welcome.
Grey-eyed Athena sent the wind astern, and the black ship ran through the dark,
past Elis and the needle islands, toward Ithaca and the ambush that waited in the strait.

OD-B15-S04.text: At dawn, friend, I'll go down to the town and beg at the great house;
perhaps the suitors need a man to carve meat and pour wine.
I refuse to eat your bread another day and give nothing back.
Tell me of old Laertes, does he still live?
And the mother of Odysseus, what became of her?
what land bore you, and how did you come to serve this house?
I was a king's son once, on the island men call Syria,
till a Phoenician woman of my father's house sold me to her traders for trinkets and a passage home.
Seven days we ran before the wind;
on the seventh she dropped dead in the hold, and they carried me on like cargo, to sell.
Laertes bought him in Ithaca and the royal household raised him.

OD-B15-S05.text: And as the ship closed on Ithaca, a hawk, Apollo's swift messenger,
swept by on the right with a dove torn in its talons, and the feathers fell between Telemachus and the sea.
The bird flew on your right hand, Telemachus, no house in Ithaca out-kings yours;
the power stays with your line forever!
Crew, take her round to the town harbor without me;
I go inland to look over my farms.
Tonight I lodge with the herdsmen, and tomorrow evening I'll set out a feast to pay you for the voyage.
Piraeus will keep you honorably, friend, until I send for you.
Trust him as you would me.

OD-B16-S01.text: Telemachus approaches Eumaeus's farm and the dogs greet him without aggression.
Light of my eyes, you came back to me.
I never thought to see you walk through that gate again.
I will find a place by the door.
For news and enters the hut beside the unknown beggar?

OD-B16-S02.text: Eumaeus to report your safe return to Penelope privately?
I take the low road and I say it to no one else.
Athena appears outside the hut, visible only to Odysseus, and signals that recognition may begin.
Odysseus follows her outside while Telemachus remains within.

OD-B16-S03.text: Athena restores Odysseus's strength, clothing, skin, and dark hair outside the hut.
Some god is standing in this hut, and I have nothing here to offer you.
Himself the father for whom Telemachus has suffered.
Telemachus embrace and weep with the force of birds robbed of their young.

OD-B16-S04.text: For the exact number of suitors?
two men cannot fight so many.
Zeus and Athena stand with us, and they are worth more than a hundred spears.
Carry every weapon out of the hall to the storeroom, and leave two swords, two spears,
two shields where our hands can reach them.
I will go back and swallow their laughter without a word.
No one hears this from me.
Let Eumaeus walk the stranger down to town when the sun is high,
and let him beg his bread there like any other.

OD-B16-S05.text: Telemachus's ship reaches harbor before the ambush vessel can intercept it.
A herald publicly announces the prince's return before Eumaeus can deliver the private message.
Argues they must seek a favorable omen first.

OD-B16-S06.text: The swineherd is on the path, and he must find nothing here but rags.
Telemachus's safe arrival and the suitors' failed ship.
A messenger from the crew reaches Penelope with the same news.
The three men eat and sleep while father and son preserve the secret.

OD-B17-S01.text: Come here, child, let me look at you.
What Nestor and Menelaus told him but withholds the plan and his father's return.
Odysseus is already in Ithaca, preparing revenge.

OD-B17-S02.text: Lean on the staff, old man.
The town road is long and my legs are older than they look.
At a fountain they meet Melanthius driving the suitors' best goats.
Is that the best you can offer, Eumaeus?
Odysseus suppresses the urge to kill him and continues toward the palace.

OD-B17-S03.text: Near the palace Odysseus sees his old dog Argos lying neglected on dung.
He lifts his head out of the dung, drops his ears, and beats his tail,
but he has no strength left to rise and come.
Eumaeus, that dog on the heap.
There is a fine shape under all that dirt.
Was he a hunter once, or only a table dog kept for show?
Twenty years he waited, and one look was enough.
The dark of death takes Argos in the moment he has seen his master again.

OD-B17-S04.text: Eumaeus enters first and Telemachus signals him to seat the beggar at the door.
Odysseus crosses his own threshold unrecognized and hears Phemius singing.
Give what you can spare, my lord.
You have plenty and it costs you nothing.
I was a rich man once with a house of my own, and I fed every wanderer who came to my door.
Man after man drops food in his bag, half from pity, half from habit.
Then Antinous rises and demands to know who let this thing in through the door.

OD-B17-S05.text: I had a house and men of my own once, and I gave to any beggar who came.
My crew were cut down along the river and I was sold from hand to hand until I came to this door.
What god dumped this plague on our dinner?
Back from the table, you shameless thing, before you find an Egypt worse than the first.
Your body is handsome, but there is no mind inside it.
Sitting in another man's house you would not give a grain of salt from a table that is not yours.
Antinous hurls a footstool into his shoulder.
Hear me, gods, and you avengers of the poor, if a beggar has any claim on heaven.
Let Antinous meet his death before his wedding day.
Even the other suitors condemn the violation of a stranger.

OD-B17-S06.text: Eumaeus to bring him for questioning?
Not now, and tell her so kindly.
There are hard hands in that hall, and one has already found me.
Let me come to her at dusk when the light is gone.
He sees these men for exactly what they are.
Let him come when the hall empties, and he will sit by my fire and say whatever he likes.
Every one of these men will meet his death.

OD-B17-S07.text: Come back at dawn with news.
Eumaeus takes leave of the disguised Odysseus and the prince without recognizing their bond.
The beggar remains in the palace under the suitors' gaze.

OD-B18-S01.text: Move away from this threshold, old man, before I drag you out by the ankle.
There is room for only one beggar here.
I have done you no harm.
Take your share and leave mine alone, or you may learn how little age tells you about a man’s hands.
Goat bellies are sizzling on our fire, friends.
The winner takes the fattest and eats with us from this night on.
The loser begs at no door of ours again.
Swear to me first that no hand in this hall strikes me from behind.
An old man cannot fight one belly and a whole house at once.

OD-B18-S02.text: Stand taller, man of many turns.
Let them see the shoulders I remember.
Odysseus chooses not to kill him and breaks his jaw with one compact blow.
Sit there in the dirt and keep the dogs and the pigs off yourself.
You were king of the beggars an hour ago.
Come back to this gate and you will not walk away from it.
Cheer and Amphinomus gives the victor food and wine.

OD-B18-S03.text: no man should become lawless in prosperity.
The master of this house is nearer than any of you believe.
I pray some god carries you home before he crosses his own threshold,
for when he comes there will be blood between him and these suitors.
Amphinomus walks away shaken, sensing danger but unable to escape Athena's design.
The warning becomes another unheeded exit offered before the slaughter.

OD-B18-S04.text: Go down among them, Penelope, and shine.
Let their knees go weak and their hands go to their treasure chests.
I will make you taller than you were and whiter than cut ivory, and wake you at the right moment.
Telemachus, your mind was steadier when you were a boy.
You let a guest be mauled under this roof, and the shame of it lies on us, not on him.
Listen, and I will tell it in order.
Odysseus's parting instructions and demands courtship gifts.
The heralds run, and back come robes and earrings and chains of worked gold.
In the shadow by the door Odysseus is smiling,
because she is stripping them of their wealth while her heart is somewhere else entirely.

OD-B18-S05.text: After Penelope withdraws, disloyal maids light the hall for the suitors.
Eurymachus, he threatens us with his master's homecoming.
The poor thing has had one cup of wine and now he is a prophet.
Stranger, that skull of yours burns brighter than the lamps, and not one hair on it.
Come work my fields for wages, and see whether you can lift a stone.
Or is begging the only trade that fills a belly without sweat?
Set the two of us in deep meadow grass in spring with good scythes, and you would not see my back all day.
Put us both in the front rank with spears and shields, and no one here would laugh at my bald head.
Eurymachus throws a stool and misses.
Telemachus rebukes the suitors and ends the night's disorder.

OD-B19-S01.text: Remove the weapons from the hall.
Athena carries a golden lamp while father and son take shields, spears, and helmets to the storeroom.
Tells Eurycleia the smoke has damaged them and you must be protected from drunken quarrels.
The hall is left apparently defenseless for the future contest.

OD-B19-S02.text: The hearth and orders Melantho to stop insulting the guest.
Tell me now, stranger, who you are and from what people.
Every man on earth has a father and a city, and I will hear yours.
Penelope describes the suitors and the shroud deception.
For proof that the stranger truly knows Odysseus?

OD-B19-S03.text: In Crete they called me Aethon, third son of Deucalion, of the line of Minos.
Your husband was driven to my shore by a north wind, and I gave him bread and dark wine for twelve days.
Odysseus describes the king's purple cloak, golden brooch, tunic, and herald Eurybates in exact detail.
Penelope weeps as if melting snow while Odysseus keeps his eyes hard despite inward grief.
The stranger truly encountered her husband.
swears Odysseus is near and will return within the month.

OD-B19-S04.text: Eurycleia, rise and wash the feet of your master's age-mate.
By now the hands and feet of Odysseus must be worn as this man's are, if he is still under the sun.
Odysseus recognizes the danger but cannot refuse without suspicion.
The nurse touches the old boar scar and instantly knows him.
Odysseus drops the foot into the basin, spilling water, and reaches toward Penelope.
Odysseus grips her throat gently but firmly and makes her swear silence.

OD-B19-S05.text: The scar triggers the story of young Odysseus visiting his grandfather Autolycus.
At dawn he hunts with his uncles on Mount Parnassus.
A boar bursts from dense cover and charges.
Odysseus spears it but receives a deep tusk wound above the knee.
The hunters bind the wound, stop the blood with a charm, and carry him home.

OD-B19-S06.text: After the secret is restored, I tells the beggar your dream of twenty geese killed by a great eagle.
In the dream the eagle speaks with Odysseus's voice and says the geese are the suitors.
There is no second reading of it, lady.
The dream has told you its own meaning, and it has named the day of their death.
she will marry the man who strings Odysseus's bow and shoots through twelve axes.
Withdraws upstairs and Athena gives her sleep.

OD-B20-S01.text: Odysseus lies awake in the portico, angered by disloyal maids slipping out to the suitors.
Why you doubts after reaching home?
I am with you, and I never leave you.
If fifty companies of men stood against us with spears, you would drive off their cattle by morning.
I lay it on your eyes myself.
Hear me, for death, and dreams that Odysseus lies beside her.

OD-B20-S02.text: Zeus for a double sign from sky and household?
Zeus thunders from a clear sky.
Hear me, that the suitors' next feast be their last.
Odysseus recognizes both signs and takes courage.

OD-B20-S03.text: Eurycleia wakes the household and servants prepare the hall for Apollo's feast day.
Do the men treat you any better today, or is the house still the house it was?
Still working the doorway for scraps?
My eyes run when I look at you.
My master would wear your rags now, if he lives.
Herdsman, mark what I say, and let the gods hear it.
Before you drive your cattle home again, Odysseus will stand in this house,
and you will see with your own eyes the suitors killed.

OD-B20-S04.text: Is that the best you can offer, the beggar and hurls an ox hoof as a guest-gift?
Continue, and to spear the offender if another assault occurs.
I will not control her choice.

OD-B20-S05.text: Athena drives the suitors into uncontrollable laughter while their meat drips blood in their vision.
They laugh with jaws that will not close, and the meat they lift is dripping blood,
and the tears run down their faces while they laugh.
Theoclymenus sees darkness covering them, ghosts crowding the court, and blood on the walls.
Announces their approaching destruction and leaves when they mock him.
Telemachus and Odysseus watch one another across the doomed feast.

OD-B21-S01.text: Athena inspires Penelope to begin the contest that will expose the suitors to slaughter.
The queen enters the storeroom, unlocks the doors, and lifts Odysseus's bow and quiver down.
Athena sits with the weapon across her knees and weeps before carrying it to the hall.
Two maids carry in the chest of iron, and the axes are set down ringing on the floor of the hall.

OD-B21-S02.text: Here is the great bow of Odysseus.
Whoever strings it with his own hands and sends an arrow clean through all twelve axes,
I will go with that man, and leave this house I came to as a bride.
Eumaeus and Philoetius weep at the sight of their master's weapon.
Take your crying outside, you fools.
Telemachus plants the axes in a straight line and tries the bow three times.
On the fourth attempt he nearly strings it, but Odysseus signals him to stop.

OD-B21-S03.text: But I tell you, this bow will take the life and the breath out of the best men here,
and better to die than live on failing at what we came for.
One after another they took it up, and braced it, and sweated, and set it down again, and the bow did not move.
Melanthius lights a fire and brings fat so the bow can be warmed and greased.
Even Eurymachus cannot string it and suffers humiliation.
Pour the wine, and we finish this tomorrow.

OD-B21-S04.text: If Odysseus walked through that gate this hour, which side would you two stand on?
The herdsmen embrace him and weep, then swear support.
Assigns Eumaeus to deliver the bow, Philoetius to lock the courtyard gate, and both to secure the women.

OD-B21-S05.text: To test your strength with the bow?
Then they roared at him, and under the anger ran a colder thing,
that a beggar might do what their hands could not.
Let the stranger have the bow.
He is a guest in my house, and no guest is refused here.
And if he strings it, I will give him a cloak and a tunic, a spear, and a sword,
and send him wherever his heart wants to go.
Eumaeus carries the bow through the shouting crowd to Odysseus.

OD-B21-S06.text: Eurycleia locks the women into their quarters at Telemachus's instruction.
Philoetius fastens the courtyard gate with a ship's cable.
Odysseus turns the bow in his hands, inspecting every part while the suitors mock him.
Every way out of that hall is closed, and the men inside it are still laughing.

OD-B21-S07.text: Odysseus strings the bow effortlessly, as a musician strings a lyre.
It is time, son of Laertes.
I have set my sign on the day.
Telemachus places sword and spear beside him and moves to his father's side.
Odysseus nocks an arrow and shoots cleanly through all twelve axes.
Tells you that the stranger has not disgraced the house and signals the next phase.

OD-B22-S01.text: Odysseus strips off his rags, leaps onto the threshold, and pours the remaining arrows before him.
Odysseus shoots Antinous through the throat while the suitor lifts a cup.
Antinous falls across the table, spilling food and wine as the room erupts.
The suitors assume an accident and search for weapons that are no longer there.
You never thought I would come home from Troy.
You ate my house, you forced my women, you courted my wife while I still lived.

OD-B22-S02.text: Antinous is dead, and he was the cause of all of it.
Take back the worth of everything we ate, and twenty oxen from each man besides.
no survivor can escape his rage.
Hold the tables against his arrows and rush him, and someone raise the town!
Odysseus shoots Eurymachus in the chest.
Amphinomus charges and Telemachus kills him with a spear.

OD-B22-S03.text: Telemachus runs to the storeroom and brings shields, helmets, and spears for Odysseus, Eumaeus, Philoetius,
I left the storeroom door standing open.
Their watchman was quicker than I was.
Four men stood armed at the threshold now, and while the arrows lasted the master kept shooting,
and man after man went down in the dust.
When the arrows run low they transition to spear combat.

OD-B22-S04.text: There is a way up to the storeroom.
Twelve shields, twelve spears, twelve helmets, and I will bring them down.
Someone is arming them out of my own storeroom.
Go up, find him, and bring me his hands tied behind his back.
Odysseus catch Melanthius returning for more arms.
Odysseus bind his hands and feet, hoist him by a rope to the rafters, and leave him suspended in pain.

OD-B22-S05.text: Odysseus, I have not forgotten you.
Remember the friend who honored you all his life.
Or have you come late on purpose, now the work is nearly done?
Odysseus rebukes him but first tests his strength by remaining disguised and partially withholding help.
Athena deflects them into walls and doors.
Then the four cast as one, and four men fell, and the hall filled with the noise of the dying.
Athena raises her aegis from the roof beam and terror breaks the remaining formation.

OD-B22-S06.text: Odysseus and his allies pursue the suitors through the hall like falcons among smaller birds.
You were their diviner, Leiodes, and you prayed often enough for my wife's hand.
There is no mercy in me for that.
Spare me, Odysseus, and pity me.
No man taught me my songs but a god, and I came into this hall under force, not for love of them.
The living search the blood-filled hall for any remaining threat.

OD-B22-S07.text: Identifies twelve maids who consorted with the suitors and mocked the household.
The women carried the bodies out under the porch,
and scoured the tables and the floor with water and sponges until the hall was clean.
No clean death for them, not by my sword.
They poured shame on my head and on my mother's while she lay alone.
They brought Melanthius down into the court and cut him apart, and gave what was left to the dogs.
So the house was emptied of its false servants,
and everything that had rotted inside it was carried out into the light.

OD-B22-S08.text: Bring sulfur and fire so the hall can be purified.
Loyal women enter, recognize him, and embrace him in tears.
Odysseus receives them while restraining grief and maintaining security.
Odysseus sends Eurycleia upstairs to wake Penelope and announce that her husband has returned.

OD-B23-S01.text: Wake, my child, wake and see it with your own eyes.
Odysseus is home, here in this house, and every suitor lies dead in the hall.
The man you have mourned twenty years is sitting by his own fire.
